scope: Fail-closed shoulder-root detail extension for H3 topology promotion
summary: New H3 candidates must now label unique left and right shoulder origins and prove that both arm roots remain outside the head/neck region on every decoded, digest-bound frame; legacy evidence remains readable but cannot promote a candidate.
evidence: The earlier generic left/right shoulder-attachment gates already rejected the observed candidate, but did not separately expose duplicate roots or head/neck-origin ambiguity.
TopologyFrameReview now supports three explicit boolean gates: unique_left_shoulder_origin, unique_right_shoulder_origin, and arm_roots_clear_of_head_and_neck.
IdentityPromotionContract adds topology_kinematic_detail and rejects incomplete legacy labels even when their nine older topology booleans pass.
The v2 review-plan schema requires all twelve semantic gates; all labels still require complete decoded-frame SHA-256 coverage.
Sixteen focused tests pass and Ruff passes after the extension.
lessons: A broad shoulder-attachment label is insufficient for diagnosing duplicated roots and arms visually emerging from the head or neck.
Backward-readable evidence and forward promotion eligibility should be separate: historical labels remain auditable without weakening the new gate.
limitations: The new gates have not yet been applied to an r3 generated video.
They are semantic 2-D judgments and do not prove a physical 3-D kinematic tree.
next_actions: Review every r3 candidate with a schema-2 plan containing all twelve gates and per-frame decoded digests.
